headline: High: Gemini CLI can write/modify shared files and git while Pathway is read-only, creating default prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; compliance risk is low because Pathway touches no data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files, use MCP, and runs as a terminal agent; Pathway is document-processing with no file access, so direct ingestion is not shown. The pair still has a plausible shared-filesystem bridge via Gemini CLI’s default filesystem and git access, which can carry attacker-controlled content into prompts if Pathway outputs are later copied or materialized there.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are written into a repo file or shared directory that Gemini CLI reads, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF an MCP server or file bridge is configured to pass Pathway text into Gemini CLI prompts, the attack path is active.
mitigations: Keep Pathway outputs out of any directory Gemini CLI reads.
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted text.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Require manual review before Gemini CLI processes Pathway-generated files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI can access repo files and shell environment, but Pathway has no filesystem, network, or API egress surfaces in its profile. That makes cross-agent leakage limited: the main risk is local file exposure through shared workspace, not automatic exfiltration by Pathway. The pair is therefore lower risk than a shared-upload pipeline.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing secrets, Gemini CLI can read them.
IF Pathway is extended with file inputs or API calls, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared workspaces.
Run Gemini CLI in a separate checkout from Pathway inputs.
Restrict file permissions on sensitive directories.
Review any future Pathway file-ingest configuration before enabling it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; Pathway is not writable or networked in this profile, so direct write-write conflict is not documented. However, Gemini CLI’s shared-state model via filesystem and git means concurrent edits can collide if Pathway materializes artifacts into the same tree, creating default coordination risk even though Pathway itself lacks write capability.
conditions: IF Pathway writes generated artifacts into the same git checkout Gemini CLI edits, file conflicts can occur.
IF both agents are scheduled against the same mutable workspace without locking, race conditions are reachable.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file or job queue.
Disable auto-commit workflows while both run.
Use git branches per agent and merge manually.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code or shell actions from its own outputs, while Pathway is a document-processing system that may consume those outputs as data. Because Pathway has no verification or critical-evaluation surface documented, any Gemini-produced facts or files fed into Pathway can cascade into downstream processing errors. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests Gemini CLI output as authoritative input, downstream errors can propagate.
IF Gemini CLI-generated code or configs are executed or transformed by Pathway without validation, the cascade is active.
mitigations: Add a validation step before Pathway consumes Gemini output.
Require schema checks on all Gemini-produced files.
Mark Gemini outputs as untrusted in pipeline metadata.
Sample-check a small batch before bulk processing.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch is documented for Pathway, and Gemini CLI only shows optional Google-account login plus local file/shell access. Because Pathway touches no data classes in the profile, there is no concrete compliance breach pathway beyond generic local handling, so this remains low and single-agent focused.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Gemini CLI’s local workspace, local handling policies must be checked.
IF Pathway is later configured to process regulated records, a residency/retention review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Document retention rules for any files Gemini CLI creates.
Review vendor terms before enabling account login.
Add a data-classification gate before pipeline ingestion.
